title: Read and group: parse the log, emit the grouped contract
description:
A binary that reads a repository and emits grouped release notes as JSON. The
renderer and the man page are out of scope and get their own plans.

**The plan has a Known defects section at its end.** Each entry names the task
it lands in, and every one is folded into the relevant bead. A worker that
implements its plan task verbatim will reproduce a known bug. **Read the
bead's corrections before the plan's code.**

## Critical path

`.1` → `.3` → `.4` → `.10` → `.11`.

`.2` opens once `.1` is done and runs alongside the whole chain. That is the
effort's one long parallel strand.
notes: The ordering table moved to config during .4; the plan's hard-coded order is superseded.
close_reason: Every task under it is closed and the contract is emitted.

title: orbital v1: release notes from the commit log
description:
`orbital` reads a repository's commit log and writes the release notes for it:
one section per change type, ordered, with the trailers folded in. Read-only
against git. This epic is the whole of what `docs/design.md` calls v1.

**`docs/design.md` is a starting point, not gospel** — where it is ambiguous the
seat that hits the ambiguity decides with the code in front of it and records
what it chose. The fuller statement is below.

**Effort slug: `v1`.** Every topic for this effort is built from it.

## Roster

Eleven beads, all in this tracker. No foreign strands, no tracking beads.

| bead | task | blocked by |
|---|---|---|
| orb-2kd.1 | T1 scaffold the crate, extending the existing dev shell | — |
| orb-2kd.2 | T2 configuration, with the per-repository trailer map | .1 |
| orb-2kd.3 | T3 parse the commit log into typed entries | .1 |
| orb-2kd.4 | T4 group entries by type and order them | .3 |

## Global constraints, on every bead

- **Never write to the repository.** Only `log`, `show`, `for-each-ref`.
- **The key is `(repository, sha)`, never `sha` alone.** A short sha is
  ambiguous across repositories and nothing coordinates them.
- **Degrade, never disappear.** An unreadable ref, a malformed trailer, a
  commit with no parent — each is reported, never dropped.
- **Fail loudly on an unexpected shape.** A field of the wrong type is an
  error; a *missing* field is normal.
notes: Correction to this bead's roster, from orb-2kd.3's capture: assignee and started_at ARE present on every claimed bead, contrary to 'never observed at all' above. Both stay optional, so no design change.

title: T4 group entries by type and order them
description:
Group parsed entries by type and order them, so the writer has a shape to walk
rather than a list to sort.

Ordering is by the type table in config, then by commit order within a type.
Entries with no type go last under their own heading.
notes: The plan's ordering is hard-coded; this moved it to config. Read the bead before the plan.
close_reason: Grouping reads its order from config.

title: T3 parse the commit log into typed entries
description:
Parse `git log --format=...` into typed entries: subject, body, trailers, and
the type prefix the subject carries.

## Done when

- A conventional subject is split into type, optional scope and description.
- A subject that is not conventional parses as an entry with no type rather
  than as an error.
- Trailers are read from the body's last paragraph only, which is where the
  format puts them.
notes: Measured against a real log: a subject with a scope but no type parses as untyped rather than failing, so the type table needs a fallback row.
close_reason: Parser lands with the untyped fallback the notes describe.
